units.function: Embedded-Postgres integration specification for blocker-aware wake admission, deferred dependency-resolution events, per-Agent concurrency queues, stale queued-run cancellation, and Issue-subtree pause handling.
units.dependencyDirection: The suite drives heartbeatService over Issue relations, tree holds, wake requests, run/execution-lock projections and Agent runtime configuration; dependency and hold policy are evaluated inside the scheduling service before a mocked adapter is invoked.
units.keyDataModels: Issue blocks relation and parent tree, IssueTreeHold mode/status/release policy, Agent heartbeat maxConcurrentRuns, AgentWakeupRequest queued/skipped/deferred states and idempotency key, HeartbeatRun queued/running/cancelled/result/error fields, Issue execution lock, and interaction context annotations.
units.lifecycle: A normal assignment to blocked Work is skipped without creating a Run, while a comment interaction may execute with unresolved-blocker context; completing a blocker permits a resolution wake, or defers it if the same Work already runs; excess Agent work remains queued; queued runs are revalidated and cancelled with their stale execution lock cleared when blockers persist; an active ancestor pause suppresses ordinary wakes at least 17 levels deep but permits a persisted human comment interaction, including under a legacy full_pause note.
units.testAssessment: Six integration cases cover blocker admission, interaction bypass, same-Work resolution deferral with idempotency, maxConcurrentRuns=1, dequeue-time dependency revalidation, execution-lock cleanup, deep tree-hold propagation and rejection of an Agent-forged comment wake. Missing are multiple/partially resolved blockers, cycles and cross-Company relations, dependency deletion/rewrite races, distributed scheduler concurrency and fairness, priority/starvation, queue expiry/cancellation, crash atomicity, lease fencing, hold release/revocation, authorization to create relations or holds, comment edits/deletion, and proof that an allowed interaction is technically restricted from tools/data mutations. The tests manually create a relation table, weakening migration/schema fidelity.
units.designRationale: Treat dependency and pause state as admission policy rather than prompt advice, re-check mutable blockers immediately before queued execution, preserve liveness when resolution occurs during a run, and keep human communication reachable even while automated work is paused.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a durable Work dependency graph, resource-aware scheduling and emergency pause controls that prevent unsafe execution without cutting off accountable-human communication or losing resumable intent.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the admission/dequeue double-check, idempotent deferred resolution, fenced per-principal concurrency limit, stale-run terminal receipt, lock cleanup and ancestor-hold projection. Separate CommunicationCapability from ExecutionCapability: a human message during a hold may update the mailbox or request review, but must not start a mutation-capable Agent runtime unless a distinct policy authorizes it. Define typed hold modes, dependency graph invariants, accountable owner, expiry/release authority, permission/data snapshots and event/outbox transitions; use a scheduler lease rather than process-local liveness.
units.responsibilityConflict: responsibleUserId is present in most fixtures but never participates in blocker, hold, resume or cancellation authority. Caller-supplied wake context helps route work, while an allowed user comment starts the same adapter execution path even under pause/full_pause without a demonstrated read-only sandbox or tool/data restriction. Relations and holds lack tested creator authorization and responsibility-contract binding, and clearing mutable Issue locks is not an immutable cancellation/decision receipt.
